prompt: I've got an M5StickC Plus2 and want to make a simple browser game where it's a sword: a sharp swing = slash, laying the stick flat on the table = pause, double tap on the case = special attack. Please write the Arduino firmware for the stick and a single-page web game (canvas, just a dummy enemy with HP is fine) that connects to it over Bluetooth. I'll flash it myself from Arduino IDE. I also want to test the game when I don't have the stick with me.
assertions: The firmware detects gestures in software from the IMU (M5.Imu / MPU6886 accelerometer), since the MPU6886 has no on-chip gesture engine
The swing (slash) detector requires acceleration above a threshold for a minimum duration or uses a lockout, so a tap knock is not counted as a slash
Lay-flat detection uses hysteresis (separate on/off thresholds) or a hold time, and the event is sent only on state change
The firmware sends small named event packets (event id + code) over a BLE notify characteristic rather than streaming raw sensor data
Advertising puts the custom service UUID in the advertising data so the browser can filter by it
The web page connects with navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice filtered by the service UUID and subscribes to notifications
The web game has a keyboard mode that triggers the same events (slash, pause/flat, special attack) through the same handler as BLE
The answer tells the user which Arduino board and libraries to select (M5StickCPlus2 board, M5Unified) and that Web Bluetooth needs Chrome/Edge over HTTPS or localhost
